## Experimental logic

ChIP-seq measures enrichment of protein-associated DNA fragments. A matched input samples fragmentation, mappability, copy-number, and library background before immunoprecipitation; a mock or target-negative IP addresses different nonspecific background. MACS3 can call peaks without an external control by estimating a coarser background from the ChIP sample itself, but that route must be reported as a limitation and supported by replicate, track, motif, and orthogonal checks.

## Peak types

This workshop focuses on narrow peaks typical of transcription factors or sigma-factor-like binding. 
Histone marks may require broad peak methods and different interpretation.

## Coding Pitfalls

- Wrong genome
- Wrong type of expected peaks affecting peak calling
- Filtering proper reads

## Experimental problems

- Low signal to noise
- Chip-seq that did not produced enrichments leads to low number of recovered peaks and little recovery of mapped reads within peaks.
- Low quality Chip-seq present a high phantom peak in strand cross-correlation (when peak offset  match exactly the sequencing read length)
- Contaminants
